title: Probability and statistical inference
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Model uncertainty, derive expectations and interpret inference without confusing significance with effect size.

blocks.deliverable: Calculate conditional and marginal probabilities from a joint model.
Normalize a distribution and calculate moments.
Compare independent and merely uncorrelated examples.
Week 7 midterm; simulate convergence and its limitations.
Compare interval coverage over repeated simulations.
Calculate power or sensitivity and examine residuals.
Report assumptions, uncertainty and reproducible code; take the final.

project: Preregister a simulated experiment, estimate an effect with uncertainty and report null results.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major result aloud without notes.
